newsitem.title: UK: Scotch whisky exports edge up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Scotch whisky exports edge up in 1996.

text.p: A rise in Scotch whisky exports to the United States and Japan during 1996 helped offset a decrease in sales within the European Union, the Scotch Whisky Association said on Wednesday.

Exports totalled 2.278 billion stg in 1996, up slightly from 2.277 billion in 1995. Growth in the United States was up six percent to 273 million stg, fuelled by a 25 percent increase in bottled-in-Scotland malt whisky exports.
Bottled-in-Scotland values also climbed in Japan which pushed the total value of exports up by eight percent to 128.8 million stg.
South Korea showed a 44 percent increase in Scotch whisky exports to 128.9 million stg, making it the fourth largest export market.
In Europe, non-European Union markets rose by 2 percent but higher taxes within the EU held back figures. Exports to France grew by two percent to 230 million stg.
Two tax rises in Greece, of 46 percent and 25 percent and one of 26 percent in Spain hampered sales of Scotch in two export markets that have shown significant growth in recent years.
Further tax rises in Italy, Sweden and Portugal further depressed markets. In Germany the market improved with exports up 16 percent to 98.3 million stg, said the Association.
The UK excise duty cuts in recent government budgets set an example which other countries would do well to follow, it said.
The UK duty cut in late 1995 boosted releases from whisky bonds by 3.4 percent raising the home market to 32 million litres of pure alcohol, equal to 114 million bottles.
